did_you_know.text: Did you know? The prophecy compares the future increase of the Israelites to the sand of the sea and promises that they will be called “children of the living God” instead of “not my people.”
Did you know? The chapter says that the people of Judah and Israel will gather together and come under one leader—an expression of unity between the two parts of the nation.
Did you know? Names of rejection are changed into names expressing belonging and compassion: “Not My People” becomes “My People,” and “Not Shown Mercy” becomes “Shown Mercy.”

Did you know? Israel is described as believing that her lovers provide her with bread, water, wool, flax, oil, and drink; however, the prophecy makes clear that the abundance is given to her by the LORD.
Did you know? One image of punishment in the chapter is the blocking of the way with thornbushes and a wall, so that the people cannot find their path.
Did you know? The prophecy emphasizes that Israel does not recognize the source of her abundance: she does not know that the LORD gave her grain, new wine, olive oil, silver, and gold.
Did you know? The wilderness, which usually symbolizes a difficult place, is presented here as a place where the LORD will speak tenderly to Israel and open a door of hope.

Did you know? In the future, Israel will call the LORD “my husband” rather than “my master”; this describes a change in both the way she addresses Him and the nature of the relationship between the LORD and Israel.

Did you know? The future covenant is described as a covenant of peace with the wild animals, the birds of the sky, and the creatures of the ground; as part of it, the bow, the sword, and war will be abolished.

Did you know? The renewed relationship between the LORD and Israel is described in the language of betrothal once again, and it is founded on righteousness, justice, steadfast love, compassion, and faithfulness.

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, a chain of responses is described: the LORD answers the heavens, the heavens answer the earth, and the earth answers the grain, the new wine, and the olive oil.
